title: Type 2 diabetes: diagnosis, targets, and choosing therapy

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on the ADA Standards of Care and standard primary care practice. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: At what haemoglobin A1c is diabetes diagnosed?
questions.why: Prediabetes runs from 5.7% to 6.4%. In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycaemia the result is confirmed by repeating it or by a second test.

questions.q: At what fasting plasma glucose is diabetes diagnosed?
questions.why: Impaired fasting glucose is 100 to 125. A random glucose of 200 or more with classic symptoms is also diagnostic on its own.

questions.q: What is the A1c target for most nonpregnant adults with diabetes?
questions.why: Under 8% is reasonable for patients with limited life expectancy, frailty or a history of severe hypoglycaemia; tighter targets suit those who can reach them without hypoglycaemia.

questions.q: Which drug is first-line for most adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and no heart or kidney disease?
questions.why: It is cheap, weight neutral, does not cause hypoglycaemia on its own, and has the longest safety record. Lifestyle change starts at the same time, not instead.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Which class is recommended regardless of A1c?
questions.why: The heart failure benefit is independent of glucose lowering, which is why the drug is indicated even when A1c is already at target.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Which classes have proven cardiovascular benefit?
questions.why: Either is recommended independent of A1c. The GLP-1 agonist has the stronger evidence for stroke, the SGLT-2 inhibitor for heart failure and kidney outcomes.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease and albuminuria. Which class slows kidney decline?
questions.why: It is recommended down to an eGFR of about 20 for kidney protection even though its glucose-lowering effect fades as eGFR falls.

questions.q: Below what eGFR should metformin be stopped?
questions.why: It should not be started between 30 and 45, and an existing dose is usually halved there. The concern is lactic acidosis when the drug accumulates.

questions.q: Which deficiency should be checked periodically in patients on long-term metformin?
questions.why: Metformin reduces B12 absorption. A neuropathy in a diabetic patient on metformin is B12 deficiency until proven otherwise.

questions.q: Which classes carry a meaningful risk of hypoglycaemia on their own?
questions.why: The other four lower glucose in a glucose-dependent way. Combining any of them with a sulfonylurea or insulin inherits that partner's hypoglycaemia risk.

questions.q: Which history is a contraindication to a GLP-1 receptor agonist?
questions.a: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2
questions.why: The warning comes from thyroid C-cell tumours in rodents. Pancreatitis history is a caution rather than an absolute bar, and nausea is the common reason patients stop.

questions.q: For how long before major surgery should an SGLT-2 inhibitor be held?
questions.why: The risk is euglycaemic ketoacidosis, which can occur with a near-normal glucose during fasting, surgery or acute illness. Sick-day rules apply for the same reason.

questions.q: At presentation, insulin is recommended from the start when A1c exceeds what?
questions.why: Also when glucose is 300 mg/dL or more, or when there are catabolic features such as weight loss or ketosis. Insulin can often be stepped back once glucotoxicity resolves.

questions.q: What is the usual starting dose of basal insulin in type 2 diabetes?
questions.a: 0.1 to 0.2 units per kg per day
options: 0.1 to 0.2 units per kg per day
questions.why: In practice that is about 10 units. It is titrated by 2 units every 3 days or so against fasting glucose, and overbasalisation is suspected above about 0.5 units per kg.

questions.q: How often should urine albumin and eGFR be checked in type 2 diabetes without known kidney disease?
questions.why: Once kidney disease is present the interval shortens to one to four times a year depending on stage, and it is the albuminuria that drives the SGLT-2 and ACE inhibitor decisions.
